title: Pages Shout, Shelves Whisper
request: This catalogue records pages in the hundreds and shelf numbers in single digits. Put both columns in standard units before measuring anything, then tell me the nearest book's genre.
objective: Scale features before measuring distance so one column cannot drown the other.
starter:

shelves = catalogue.column('shelf')
page_units = (pages - np.mean(pages)) / np.std(pages)
shelf_units = (shelves - np.mean(shelves)) / np.std(shelves)
gaps = np.sqrt((page_units - stranger.item(0)) ** 2 + (shelf_units - stranger.item(1)) ** 2)

hints: A hundred pages and a hundred shelves are not the same journey.
Convert the pages column and the shelf column to standard units, and convert the stranger with the very same means and spreads.
Measure the straight-line distance in those standard units, sort, and deliver the first genre.
inputCode:
import random
from datascience import Table, make_array
count = random.randint(5, 9)
same_scale = random.choice([True, False, False])
pages = random.sample(range(100, 900), count) if not same_scale else random.sample(range(1, 10), count)
shelves = random.sample(range(1, 10), count)
kinds = [['picture', 'history', 'poetry'][i % 3] for i in range(count)]
catalogue = Table().with_columns('pages', make_array(*pages), 'shelf', make_array(*shelves), 'genre', make_array(*kinds))
stranger = make_array(random.choice(pages) + random.randint(-40, 40), random.randint(1, 9))
del count, same_scale, pages, shelves, kinds
reference:
import numpy as np
pages = catalogue.column('pages')
shelves = catalogue.column('shelf')
page_units = (pages - np.mean(pages)) / np.std(pages)
shelf_units = (shelves - np.mean(shelves)) / np.std(shelves)
asked_pages = (stranger.item(0) - np.mean(pages)) / np.std(pages)
asked_shelf = (stranger.item(1) - np.mean(shelves)) / np.std(shelves)
gaps = np.sqrt((page_units - asked_pages) ** 2 + (shelf_units - asked_shelf) ** 2)
deliver(catalogue.with_column('gap', gaps).sort('gap').column('genre').item(0))
